pageDescription: Numbers communicate critical data like metrics, prices, and status updates. Follow these rules to keep numeric data readable, consistent, and localized.

sections.title: Thousands Separator
bullets: Use a thousands separator in numbers to differentiate the thousands from the hundreds to improve scannability.

examples.label: Format in metric cards
examples.imageAlt: Metric card showing 2,450 / 4,000 hrs with comma thousands separator

examples.label: Format in data tables
examples.imageAlt: Data table showing TSN and TSO values with comma thousands separators

sections.title: Truncated Abbreviated Values
bullets: Use “K” for numbers in the thousands (e.g., 1,500 → 1.5K).
Use “M” for numbers in the millions (e.g., 2,000,000 → 2M).
Use “B” for numbers in the billions (e.g., 3,000,000,000 → 3B).

Include up to one decimal place for precision when necessary (e.g., 4,250 → 4.3K). To be discussed with users during design sprints and any deviation will have to be recorded in the respective service’s user story document.
